scope: Flame spread over paper in microgravity
description: The highest spread hazard is at intermediate forced-flow velocities, within the Shuttle ventilation range (8-20 cm/s): there the flame can spread faster than in normal gravity.
file_name: NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf
quote: Again, the maxi- mum fire hazard for paper appears to be at intermediate forced-flow velocities attained in low gravity (in the range of current Shuttle ventilation veloci- ties).
citation: [Source: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf, p. 10]

scope: Flammability of thin materials (paper) in microgravity with intermediate forced flow
description: In microgravity with intermediate flow, paper can burn with O2 as low as 15%, below the flammability limit measured in normal gravity.
file_name: NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf
quote: Under these conditions, the material may burn at oxygen concentrations as low as 15 percent, which is below the measured downward-spread flammability limit in normal gravity with no forced convection.
citation: [Source: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf, p. 10]

description: Baseline atmosphere = sea-level air; higher concentrations make materials more flammable. The 21% (20.95%) value is the standard air composition: the document cites 'sea-level air' without stating the number.
file_name: NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf
quote: The Shuttle currently uses standard sea-level air as its baseline atmosphere, although an elevated oxygen atmosphere is introduced in preparation for extravehicular activities.
citation: [Source: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf, p. 9]

description: An inert gas that retains 6% O2 can effectively be fire-safe; the document gives no upper limit beyond 6%.
file_name: NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf
quote: In spacecraft practice, an inert gas retaining 6 percent or greater oxygen concentration may be effec- tively fire-safe.
citation: [Source: SAFETY | NASA_Fire Safety Applications for Spacecraft NASA.pdf, p. 12]
